## Investigation summary

**Bottom line:** One root cause. The degradation originates in the data-access path of a single `ts-route-service` pod, `ts-route-service-74bff65895-m8tk7`. Its database calls intermittently stall, and that latency propagates to every caller that reaches route-service.

### Affected endpoints (abnormal vs. normal)
| Entry point (via ts-ui-dashboard / loadgenerator) | Abnormal latency | Normal |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/v1/adminrouteservice/adminroute | ~5.0 s avg (p95 ~7 s) | ~9 ms |
| GET /api/v1/routeservice/routes | ~2.7 s | ~9 ms |
| GET /api/v1/admintravelservice/admintravel | ~3.2 s | ~30 ms |
| POST /api/v1/travelplanservice/travelPlan/minStation | ~1.7 s | — |
| POST /api/v1/preserveservice/preserve | ~1.1 s | — |
| routeplan `routePlan/*` (minStop, quickest) | up to ~2 s | — |
| travel `admin_trip` / `trips/left` | ~1.9 s / ~0.2 s | — |

Unaffected: basic-info, admin-order, and user login/auth paths all match their normal latency.

### Origin (root cause)
- **ts-route-service pod m8tk7**: its DB spans (`SELECT ts.route`, `SELECT ts.route_distances`, `SELECT ts.route_stations`, `RouteRepository.findById/findAll/findByIds`) are normally about 0.1–0.5 ms. In the incident window, about 25% of them stall in quantized steps of roughly 200 ms and 400 ms (max ~3.3 s). The median rises to about 3 ms and p95 to about 420 ms. The stalls are steady across every minute of the window, so this is not a one-off spike.
- Pod resources do not explain it. CPU is actually lower than normal, memory is flat (~583 MB), and there are no network errors. Network I/O is roughly 2x, which is worth noting but not conclusive.
- Only this pod is affected. All route-service DB spans come from m8tk7.

### Propagation (victims, not origins)
- ts-route-service (m8tk7) → ts-admin-route-service, ts-route-plan-service, ts-travel-service, ts-travel2-service, ts-basic-service. Each of these shows client-side latency that matches its server-side call into route-service.
- ts-travel-service and ts-travel2-service have normal internal spans (~0.4 ms). Their slowness is entirely inherited from route-service.
- ts-route-plan-service → ts-travel-service and ts-travel-plan-service → ts-route-plan-service carry the same inherited latency up the chain to ts-ui-dashboard and the loadgenerator.

### Ruled out / noise
- Logs: the "Route not found" ERRORs on route-service, the verification-code "Cookie not found" WARNs, and the travel-plan "No Content" WARNs also appear at similar levels in the normal baseline. They don't explain the latency.
- Travel-service pods and CPU/memory metrics show no saturation.

### Limits
- The telemetry has no database-side metrics (lock waits, connection-pool stats, DB CPU), so I can't tell whether the ~200 ms-quantized stalls come from the route pod's connection pool or from the database itself. The fault is localized to m8tk7's DB path either way.
- I found no evidence of a second independent fault.
